newsitem.title: USA: Plan on Boston convention center released - report.
newsitem.headline: Plan on Boston convention center released - report.

text.p: The proposed $645 million convention center in Boston would generate $436 million annually of spending and create around 6,800 new jobs in the state, according to a study.
But the report, done by private consultants for state and city officials, leaves unanswered who would pay for the 600,000 square foot center and who would manage it, Boston Herald reported Tuesday.

The new cost is higher than the previous figure of $500 million given in severl convention center bills. The new price includes $50 million to acquire land for future expansion, according to the newspaper said.

Massachusetts politicians remained sharply divided over the convention center. Mass. House Speaker Thomas Finneran told the Herald that at least half the cost of a new convention center should be footed by new taxes on hotels, rental cars and other businesses which would benefit from it.
"I'm not prepared to jettison higher education or K-12 schools or highways to try to get a convention center," he was quoted as saying.
